newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00-3.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 2.00-3.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 to 3.00 cents a lb higher on Monday, after a better-than-expected performance in the London robusta market overnight, traders said.

LIFFE coffee prices gapped lower at the outset but failed to meet pre-opening expectations of $20-$30 down. By midsession Monday, robusta futures were mainly weaker, but well off session lows. May delivery was down $5 at the midday break, to $1,559 a tonne, but above the low of $1,540.

Friday, New York arabica futures ended mostly lower, after a late sell-off led by commission houses. Spot May delivery fell 1.95 cents per lb on the day, to 189.10 cents, after trading from 194.80 to 187.50. Second-month July settled 1.60 cents lower, at 172.20 cents, while the back months closed down 2.10 to up 1.10.
The May/July switch narrowed to 16.90 cents, from 17.25 cents at the close on Thursday.
After Friday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags, to 81,078 bags as of April 10. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after the close Friday, the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 8 showed non-commercial long positions decreased by 1,406 lots, to 6,493, while non-commercial short positions decreased by 1,843 lots, to 749 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 2,032 lots, to 11,810 lots and commercial short fell by 1,768 lots, to 20,896 lots.
Nonreportable long positions declined in the two weeks by 897 lots, to 12,676 lots, while nonreportable short positions fell by 724 lots, to 9,334 lots.
